title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: In Borena and East Hararghe, climate‑resilient livelihood and food‑system improvements progressed through the S4Nut programme, which expanded drought‑tolerant cropping, diversified production and strengthened nutrition‑sensitive practices, helping households maintain food availability during repeated climatic shocks. preparedness for food‑ and nutrition‑related hazards improved as communities adopted earlier, risk‑informed adjustments to planting, livestock management and water use, enhancing their capacity to withstand seasonal shocks. In Addis Ababa and Hawassa, multi‑sectoral livelihood support delivered through the Graduation Approach by MCMDO and Centre of Concern enabled ultra poor households to stabilise income, strengthen assets and improve nutrition behaviours. . Integrating actions focused on crop and livestock sub-systems to build adaptive, sustainable livelihoods and food security. This includes nutrition and climate smart crop and livestock production and market systems development for climate resilient jobs and enterprises. Nutrition Impact & Positive Practice (NIPP) and Community Conversations are being rolled out, aiming to increase health-seeking and positive nutrition behaviours, while increasing dietary diversity, especially among children. These SBC interventions are complemented by partnerships with private sector partners to support the production of nutrient dense and fortified foods e.g. via seed inputs.
